title.narrative: Provision of integrated lifesaving health services to communities likely to experience drought due to La NIna in Wanla wein district of Lower Shabelle region of South West State

description.narrative: ltpgtThe acute malnutrition situation remains dire, with an estimated 1.2 million children under the age of five across Somalia facing acute malnutrition in 2024. South West State is particularly affected, showing some of the highest rates of malnutrition, with several districts expected to experience Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) rates above the emergency threshold of 15%. Health systems in the region are overwhelmed, with limited capacity to provide adequate nutrition and healthcare services. This is compounded by disease outbreaks such as cholera and measles, which further aggravate the health status of already vulnerable populations, particularly children, pregnant and lactating women, and the elderly. The most recent situation report from UNOCHA (June 2024) highlights that humanitarian needs in South West State continue to rise, with over 3.9 million people in need of urgent assistance across Somalia. The impact of climate shocks, including recurrent droughts and erratic rainfall patterns, continues to devastate local agricultural production, livestock health, and water availability. This has significantly diminished livelihoods and increased displacement, further straining local communities and their coping mechanisms. The lack of access to clean water and adequate sanitation also worsens the risk of waterborne diseases, which disproportionately affect children and women. ltspangtThe proposed project will support 2 health Centre, 1 Primary Health Units and 2 mobile site in Wanla weyn district. NWO plans to deliver an integrated package of promotive, preventive, and curative maternal, newborn child health services and scale-up outbreak early warning and response and case management of epidemic-prone diseases through the static and mobile response team as part of the efforts to support the people likely to be affected by La Nina in Wanla weyn. The project aims to scale up the static and mobile clinics in Wanla weyn IDP, host community giving more focus to the people living in the rurals. New-Ways through this project will provide medical supplies to established health facilities, establish referral mechanisms and improve the coverage of measles vaccinations and support safe motherhood while also ensuring readiness to prevent and respond to outbreaks such as malaria, measles or AWD/Cholera and promote health update through health education and beneficiary sensitization including management of rape and GBV. The project will engages People Living With Disability, minority groups and women and girls by ensuring representation, allow access, direct engagement, collaborate, train, and engage them as staff and beneficiaries.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtThe activities to be undertaken will be in line with the EPHS standard and in an integrated with other sectors such as Nutrition and WASH will include:lt/pgtltpgtProvide Outpatient consultations to people at risk of being affected by La Nina in Wanla weyn districtltbrgtProvide routine and campaign immunization to children under 5 and TT to Women of Child Bearing AgeltbrgtEnsure the treatment of common diseases such as pneumonia, diarrhoea/dehydration, malaria, and skin conditionsltbrgtProvide Antenatal and Post-natal to pregnant and lactating mothers in all the centres.ltbrgtMaintain and continue the services being provided at the 2 H/Centre, 1 PHU and 2 Mobile sites.ltbrgtConduct a community awareness-raising workshop at the start of the project for 100 peopleltbrgtRehabilitate 2 Health CentresltbrgtProcure Medical supplies, Medical equipment.ltbrgtProvision of quality multi-sectoral services (clinical case management, PSS, justice, safety)ltbrgtConduct quarterly supervision every 3 months for three quarterslt/pgtltpgtltspangtTraining of staff and CHWs on IMCI, BeMONC, CMR and MHPSS/AWD/Choleralt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtCommunity awareness sessions held targeting 27,500 persons for a period of 8 monthslt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtEstablishment of CTU and furnish with basic requirements in anticipatory for La Ninaltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtPurchase of Medical supplies for the CTU specifically manageing AWD/Choleralt/pgtltpgtNB: All the activities will be done inline with the EPHS guidelineslt/pgt
